The Endangered Species Act (ESA) establishes a comprehensive framework for the conservation of species that are at risk of extinction, as well as the ecosystems upon which they depend. Its primary legal implication is the imposition of a duty on federal agencies to ensure that any actions they authorize, fund, or carry out do not jeopardize the continued existence of any species listed as threatened or endangered, nor do they destroy or adversely modify designated critical habitat. This requirement, often referred to as the "Section 7 consultation" process, mandates that federal agencies consult with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service or the National Marine Fisheries Service before proceeding with projects that may affect listed species. The goal is to prevent federal actions from contributing to the extinction of vulnerable species and to promote their recovery.

Regarding your question about the day that comes after Monday: Tuesday.
